changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 128 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 32 => (([0xf2bc7573, 0x59092a9d, 0xc443c8c2, 0x1d58483a, 0x1b7982bb, 0xa8882290, 0x74d0fd25, 0x00041402, 0x6879a8a5, 0xd65a6f1a, 0x7455fba3, 0x24508c1a, 0x3050a010, 0x68658ad5, 0x10a00735, 0x5e55690e, 0x6ab804a4, 0x00b01458, 0xf447af40, 0x00b07351, 0xa88c2290, 0x40d9d7bc, 0x40241486, 0x54058082, 0x6891afb9, 0x50ddf79e, 0x553080be, 0x28c180f8, 0x6ac8ae9e, 0xa6860e80, 0x20508c18, 0x10f01050] : List ℕ).getD u.val 0).testBit v.val) C
changed.unlocks: a circuit under the count we hold for this graph; how low the count goes is what we want to learn
changed.context: We hold 255 gates for this table: one AND of two ORs for each key, all ORed. Only the gate list is checked. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
changed.sketch: Row u of the table, as a hex number, is entry u of the list in the statement; bit v is set when row u is joined to column v. The table comes from a keyed mixing rule of ours (k = 5). We hold 255 gates: for each key, the OR of its rows AND the OR of its columns, all ORed; sharing those ORs between keys brings ours to 225 (computed). Answer with a gate list; it is checked by one evaluation per promise input (1024). Any method. A prover can use represents_of_pcols in lean/PEqualNP/Library/Helpers/PromiseCol.lean. At 128, four gates a side-vertex: truth unknown to us.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 32435687 (the crown with one cell removed) has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 9 gates on the promise
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun (u : Fin 5) (v : Fin 5) => (32435687 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: whether one named graph breaks the open pair's line with NOT gates
changed.context: A search. We hold a circuit with NOT gates of 11: one NOT over a circuit for the complement, which costs 10 on paper; that move cannot do better. What a circuit of 9 with NOT gates decides: with no AND/OR circuit of 14 it breaks the open pair at n = 5 (a saving of 15 - 9 = 6 against a bar of 5); with one, the graph is on the line. The floor with NOT gates we hold is 8 (a checked row). We hold no circuit of 9 gates with NOT gates; this is a search.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 39737 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 8 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (39737 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 8
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 9 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 8; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 1. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 6375855 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 10 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 10 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (6375855 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 11 gates, a weak hand form (best over a few point orders and the complement plus a NOT, equal gates merged): OR(2,3), NOT(6), AND(4,7), OR(0,1), NOT(9), AND(5,10), OR(1,2), AND(3,12), OR(8,11), OR(13,14), NOT(15) (inputs 0-5 are the points, gate k is wire 6 + k, output last). We hold no circuit of 10 gates; this is a search. No complete search of ours has run at six points.

changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it.
